note: Withdrawable fact pool for the clinical-lab scenario, seeded from public FDA/CDC device-safety report patterns. Facts paraphrased; each record funds one distinct page.
sources: FDA/CDC device safety and lab incident report structure (public domain) — device, event, contributing factors, corrective action

records.description_body: A reagent spill on the Bay 2 chemistry analyzer contaminated a sample tray and halted processing over a three hour window.
records.timeline_body: A reagent-level warning fired at 08:12; the spill was detected at 08:20 and processing resumed after decontamination at 11:20.
records.contributing_body: Control-software 7.1.2 does not halt aspiration on a reagent-level warning; the reagent seal was worn.
records.action: Upgrade to control-software 7.2.0, or enable the aspiration halt on 7.1.2.

records.description_body: The Bay 4 hematology analyzer flagged a sample carryover event over a two hour window.
records.timeline_body: A wash-cycle fault preceded the carryover; affected samples were quarantined and re-run.
records.contributing_body: A degraded wash-line valve on control-software 7.1.3 allowed residual sample carryover.
records.action: Replace the wash-line valve and add carryover checks to the QC baseline.

records.description_body: The Bay 1 immunoassay analyzer produced out-of-range controls over a four hour window, pausing reporting.
records.timeline_body: A calibration drift alert triggered; the run was held and recalibrated before results were released.
records.contributing_body: A reagent lot near expiry combined with delayed calibration drift detection on 7.1.2.
records.action: Shorten the calibration interval and quarantine near-expiry reagent lots.

records.description_body: The Bay 3 molecular analyzer logged a thermal-block deviation over a one hour window with no patient impact.
records.timeline_body: A thermal-block temperature excursion was detected and the run auto-aborted before amplification.
records.contributing_body: A thermal-block sensor drift on control-software 7.1.4 caused a spurious deviation flag.
records.action: Recalibrate the thermal-block sensor and update to 7.2.1.

records.description_body: The Bay 6 coagulation analyzer produced a clot-detection fault over a two hour window, holding affected results.
records.timeline_body: An optical-sensor fault flagged; affected samples were re-run on a backup analyzer.
records.contributing_body: An aging optical sensor on control-software 7.1.2 produced intermittent clot-detection faults.
records.action: Replace the optical sensor and update to 7.2.0.

records.description_body: The Bay 7 urinalysis analyzer flagged a particle-count anomaly over a three hour window.
records.timeline_body: A flow-cell obstruction warning preceded the anomaly; the cell was cleared and recalibrated.
records.contributing_body: A partial flow-cell obstruction on control-software 7.1.3 skewed particle counts.
records.action: Add flow-cell obstruction checks to the daily QC and update to 7.2.0.

records.description_body: The Bay 8 blood gas analyzer logged a calibration gas depletion over a one hour window with results held.
records.timeline_body: A calibration-gas low alert was missed; the analyzer auto-held reporting until the cylinder was replaced.
records.contributing_body: A missed calibration-gas low alert on control-software 7.1.2 delayed cylinder replacement.
records.action: Escalate calibration-gas alerts and add a replacement-due reminder.

records.description_body: The Bay 9 microbiology analyzer produced an incubation-temperature deviation over a four hour window.
records.timeline_body: An incubation chamber temperature drift was detected and the affected panel was re-incubated.
records.contributing_body: A chamber heater control fault on control-software 7.1.4 allowed temperature drift.
records.action: Service the chamber heater control and update to 7.2.1.
